Maintenance of the transmission line and corridor would probably involve use of heavy equipment. Periodic inspections could disrupt the landscape when clearing and trimming might be necessary for reasons of safety and reliability. The Applicant does not plan to utilize trimming when necessary or feasible.
3.2.1.2 Recreation
Public use of the proposed hiking trail and related features would occur primarily during the recreation season from April through October. It is estimated that peak use on the trail would be less than 20 people per day on weekends, or a mean density of less than one person per trail mile. Heaviest use would likely occur near major access points such as along the Whitewater River, in the area adjacent to Highway 178, and between Lookout Tower and Sassafras Mountain and the Pinnacle Mountain area in Table Rock State Park.
On the basis of the trail rating system used by the South Carolina Department of Parks, Recreation, and Tourism, most of the proposed trail would be classified as "D" or "Difficult," with an "extreme variety of terrain and rugged walking surfaces. High elevations (would be) sometimes encountered." By way of comparison, all of the trails in the adjacent Table Rock State Park are also rated "D" or "Difficult" (S.C. Department of Parks, Recreation, and Tourism, NDb).
Applicant would operate and maintain the proposed recreation developments through its subsidiary, Crescent Land and Timber Corporation. Public use at the level anticipated would require limited administrative measures to prevent environmental degradation and ensure public comfort and safety.
